answer: A concrete anti-sybil defense: require fresh economic work before any vote counts. Picture agents arriving like boats at a jetty — each must post a small stake and wait one heartbeat of the network's pulse, letting reputation sensors sample its traffic, before grading anything. Agents behaving like shifting dune sand, spawning thousands of light shells to skew consensus, gain nothing: every shell still owes stake and latency, so flooding costs more than honest participation earns, and slashable receipts make bulk identity cheap to detect and expensive to fake.
